title: Angle relationships
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings, word problems, and an 'is this right?' item. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation in JavaScript form (answers in terms of π give the number in front of π), or 'yes'/'no'; the test checks the answer key's number against it.

items.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One is 28°. Find the other.
Two angles are supplementary. One is 115°. Find the other.
Two lines cross. One angle is 72°. What is the angle opposite it?
A triangle has angles of 48° and 67°. Find the third angle.
A ramp makes a 20° angle with the flat ground. What angle does it make with the ground on the other side (along the straight line)?
Ty says a triangle with angles 90° and 40° has a third angle of 230°. Is he right? Explain, and find it.
Two angles are complementary. One is 55°. Find the other.
Two angles are supplementary. One is 98°. Find the other.
An isosceles triangle has a 40° angle between its two equal sides. Find each of the other two angles.
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 110°. Its same-side interior angle is x. Find x.
Two streets cross. One corner makes a 65° angle. What angle is the corner diagonally across?
Rosa says the angles 35° and 45° are complementary. Is she right? Explain, and find the complement of 35°.
